root_cause.text: The AMD IOMMU PCI reverse-lookup helper `__rlookup_amd_iommu()` indexed `pci_seg->rlookup_table[devid]` without validating that `devid` was within the IVRS-described range, allowing an out-of-bounds read for PCI devices not covered by the table.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (devid > pci_seg->last_bdf) return NULL;` immediately before `return pci_seg->rlookup_table[devid];`, and the CVE description states that `__rlookup_amd_iommu()` “indexes `rlookup_table[devid]` with no bounds check of its own,” so devices whose BDF is not described by the IVRS could read past the end of the allocation before the caller’s later check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent out-of-bounds AMD IOMMU reverse lookup for devices not covered by IVRS.
intent_record.what: The function __rlookup_amd_iommu() was changed so that, after matching the PCI segment ID, it now skips non-matching segments with continue, adds a check that devid is not greater than pci_seg->last_bdf, returns NULL if it is, and only then indexes pci_seg->rlookup_table[devid].
intent_record.how: At runtime, the lookup now avoids reading past the valid device range for a PCI segment when IVRS does not describe every device on the bus, preventing out-of-bounds access or invalid table lookups and returning no IOMMU mapping for undeclared devices.

There is no bounds check on `devid` before indexing the per-segment table, which matches the root cause of an out-of-bounds read when a PCI device is not covered by the IVRS-described range. The code only selects the matching segment with `if (pci_seg->id == seg)`, but does not validate that `devid` is within the valid table range.
